c0010: SETUP — Arrival at the Vending Spot
c0012: Park and level the truck (wheel chocks if needed): only in a legal vending spot under your city's rules, or with the owner's written permission on private property
c0015: Hook up the generator or event power: generator outside the truck, away from the window, air intakes and people (carbon monoxide), where the organizer and fire marshal allow; route cords so no one trips
c0018: Check propane pressure and cylinders: secured upright, valves closed in transit; system per NFPA 58 and your fire marshal's inspection
c0021: Put out the awning and outdoor signage
c0023: Set up the service counter and checkout point
c0025: Turn on the flat-top griddle, fryer and oven and check temperatures; hood and fire suppression system working first. Gas smell: light nothing, close the cylinder, get out and call 911 from outside
c0026: Plug in cold equipment (cooler, refrigerated prep table): 41 °F or below, frozen 0 °F or below (FDA Food Code 3-501.16) — log reading: ____ °F
c0027: Organize mise en place for a tight workspace
c0029: Check full stock: proteins, bread, sauces, sides
c0030: Set out sauce dispensers and napkin holders
c0031: Set up the plating / to-go packaging station
c0034: Post the menu where customers can see it (menu board, banner, screen)
c0035: Set up the POS, card reader and starting bank (cash float)
c0036: Set up the waiting area with napkin holders and a trash can
c0037: Check water: fresh (potable) water tank full, wastewater (gray water) tank empty (it must be at least 15% larger than the fresh tank, FDA Food Code 5-401.11); hot water at the handwashing sink, 100 °F or above (FDA Food Code 5-202.12)
c0040: Turn off cooking equipment and close the propane cylinder valves
c0042: Leftovers: cool from 135 °F to 70 °F within 2 h and to 41 °F within 4 more h (FDA Food Code 3-501.14), cover, date-mark (7 days max at 41 °F, day 1 = prep day; FDA Food Code 3-501.17), log and refrigerate at the commissary
c0043: Clean the flat-top griddle, fryer and work surfaces, then sanitize with an approved sanitizer at label strength, checked with test strips (FDA Food Code 4-501.114)
c0044: Empty and clean the water and waste tanks: wastewater only at the commissary or an approved servicing area, never in the street, on the ground or down a storm drain (FDA Food Code 5-402.14)
c0045: Pack up the awning, signage and outdoor furniture
c0046: Close out the cash drawer and log the day's sales: cash count and over/short against the POS Z report (card sales without tips); tips per your written tip pool policy, with no managers or supervisors in the pool (FLSA, 29 U.S.C. 203(m)(2)(B))
c0048: Shut down the generator / disconnect power
c0049: Secure the truck for the road: doors, equipment, propane cylinders strapped in with valves closed
c0065: Enough fuel for the round trip
c0067: Tire pressure correct (extra load from equipment)
c0069: Lights, turn signals and brakes working
c0070: Vehicle registration and title current with your state DMV and commercial auto insurance in force; vehicle safety inspection only where your state requires one; CDL only if GVWR is 26,001 lb or more (49 CFR 383.91)
c0073: Fire extinguishers accessible and tagged (required): one ABC plus a Class K for the fryer (NFPA 10); monthly visual check and annual service tag (29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2)-(3)); hood suppression system every 6 months (NFPA 96)
c0077: Generator fuel level (gasoline, diesel or propane, per the unit); refuel only with the generator off and cool, as its manual says
c0078: Test-start the generator before leaving (no surprises at the event)
c0079: Extension cords in good condition, connections secure
c0080: Preventive maintenance: oil, filter, spark plugs (per the manufacturer's service hours)
c0082: Propane cylinders: enough for the shift, secured upright, valves closed in transit (NFPA 58 and your fire marshal's inspection)
c0083: Gas connections leak-free: soapy-water test, never a flame, at every connection and after each cylinder swap (NFPA 1 / NFPA 58, per the edition your fire marshal uses)
c0086: Fresh water tank full (capacity per your permit): potable water from an approved source (FDA Food Code 5-101.11), filled at the commissary with a food-grade drinking-water hose used for nothing else
c0087: Wastewater tank empty and clean: dump only at the commissary or an approved servicing area, never on the ground or down a storm drain (FDA Food Code 5-402.14)
c0091: Used cooking oil container (if you have a fryer), closed, for a licensed recycler or the commissary's
c0093: Event waste plan: trash, grease and wastewater go to the commissary or the area the organizer assigns; nothing on the ground or down a storm drain (FDA Food Code 5-402.14)

c0110: Hot food held at 135 °F or above (FDA Food Code 3-501.16), or time as a public health control with a written procedure: time-marked, served or discarded within 4 h (FDA Food Code 3-501.19) — log reading: ____ °F
c0112: Thaw in the refrigerator at 41 °F or below, under cold running water at 70 °F or below, in the microwave if cooked right away, or as part of cooking (FDA Food Code 3-501.13); NEVER at room temperature
c0116: Handwashing sink stocked: hot water at 100 °F or above (FDA Food Code 5-202.12), soap and paper towels; hand sanitizer only AFTER washing, never instead (FDA Food Code 2-301.16)
c0118: No bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food: gloves, tongs or deli paper (FDA Food Code 3-301.11); fresh gloves when switching tasks
c0120: Clean surfaces, then sanitize with an approved sanitizer at label strength, checked with test strips (FDA Food Code 4-501.114)
c0123: Keep raw and cooked foods apart in storage and prep
c0128: Lidded foot-pedal trash can, emptied often

c0137: Food handler cards current for the whole crew (per your state) and a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM, e.g. ServSafe Manager) as person in charge (FDA Food Code 2-102.12)

c0141: General liability insurance current; many events ask for a certificate of insurance (COI) naming the organizer as additional insured

c0158: Commercial auto insurance for the truck

c0167: Confirm the power hookup or the need for a generator
c0168: Estimate sales volume and prep stock to match

c0232: Reach out to new event organizers and markets
